decisions.question: D1 cites topology-dsl@v1 three times: twice in the first alternative ('Topology is topology-dsl@v1's abstract base class', 'an amend topology-dsl@v1') and once in point 5 ('topology-dsl@v1 did not change'). Which are live?

options.label: the alternative's two are live, point 5's is historical
options.consequence: The alternative's reasoning, which still explains why the decision stands, cites topology-dsl@v2; point 5 keeps v1 as the account of the 2026-10-18 amendment; the note records both.

options.label: all three are live
options.consequence: Point 5 would say topology-dsl@v2 did not change on 2026-10-18, a date before v2 existed.

options.label: all three are historical
options.consequence: The alternative would keep a present-tense statement about a superseded contract.

decisions.why: The record keeps the version a historical passage describes and moves live citations. Point 5 is a dated account of an amendment hsdd-reconcile applied on 2026-10-18 while v1 was current. The alternative states in the present tense why the annotation would cost more, which still holds against topology-dsl@v2 (Topology is still its abstract base class; adding the annotation would still be an amend of the current topology-dsl). decisions.question: Does D1's upstream mark (Spec §6.5 names a `@Topology` registration mechanism, which Dart cannot declare under that name) end entirely now that Guide Appendix C.1 describes the explicit list, or does a narrowed mark stay on the `@Topology` name?

options.label: end the mark
options.consequence: Spec §6.5's 'a `@Topology` registration mechanism per platform; see Guide Appendix C' is met on Dart by C.1's explicit list, so nothing is left to upstream for this point; the wording stays as the Specification wrote it.

options.label: keep a narrowed mark on the name
options.consequence: Records that the Spec still names an annotation Dart cannot declare as `@Topology`; a mark with no practical consequence, since the Guide now names the mechanism Dart uses.

decisions.why: The H17 prompt says the Guide's description ends D1's upstream mark for that point while Spec §6.5's wording stays, and the record lists DEC-365 as adopted by Guide Appendix C.1. On reading: §6.5 already says the mechanism is per platform and defers to Guide Appendix C, and C.1 now gives the explicit list for platforms without reflection, so the name reads as the Specification's label for the per-platform mechanism. The signal that would have changed my mind: §6.5 requiring an annotation by name, which it does not.
evidence: Guide Appendix C.1 'Platforms without runtime reflection'

decisions.question: Where and how does D1 carry the note on Guide Appendix C.1, and does it state where D1 differs from the Guide's description?

options.label: a dated paragraph after the Corrected paragraph, a pointer at the mark, and the differences stated
options.consequence: D1's points stay as decided; a reader of the alternative sees that the mark ended; the note says the list lives in tool/ rather than a test and that claims are recognized rather than listed, so nobody reads C.1's 'lists its publisher claims' as a gap.

options.label: rewrite the alternative's upstream sentence in place
options.consequence: Shorter, but loses the record of the mark DEC-365 made, which the ledger and the intake cite.

options.label: a dated paragraph claiming a plain match
options.consequence: Simpler, but C.1 says the application lists its publisher claims, typically in a test, and D1 does neither; a later reader would find the mismatch unexplained.

decisions.chosen: a dated paragraph after the Corrected paragraph, a pointer at the mark, and the differences stated
decisions.why: The file already records changes to D1 as a dated bold paragraph ('Corrected 2026-10-18'), and S85 wrote its v0.15.1 notes as 'Checked 2026-10-21' paragraphs that say what was first written. The two differences are within the Guide's informative description ('typically in a test'), and recognizing claims statically is stronger than a list: every claim site in application code is seen, and nidana-checks@v1 G18 makes the catalog's claims the scan's. Orphan and unreachable-topic analysis, which C.1 says needs the full walk, is already v2 under root D1.

decisions.question: S72 observed that topic-codegen@v1 Registration point 2 and D1 point 2 say the static graph matches activation only when the registration passes 'what the app's bootstrap passes', while under bus-api@v2 G42 MODULE and PAGE topologies are never activated during bootstrap. Does this touch sharpen D1 point 2?

options.label: leave D1 point 2 as written and report it
options.consequence: D1 point 2 keeps the wording of topic-codegen@v1 Registration point 2, which it says 'the amended contract says so'; a sharpening, if wanted, lands in both in one compatible pass.

options.label: sharpen D1 point 2 alone
options.consequence: D1 says 'wherever the app constructs the topologies it activates, at bootstrap or, for MODULE and PAGE, after start()'; D1 and the contract then word one rule two ways.

options.label: sharpen it inside the v0.15.1 note

decisions.chosen: leave D1 point 2 as written and report it
decisions.why: The phrase is not false under the intended reading (the app calls one factory from both places, which point 2 says), and no v0.15.1 landing reaches it: Spec v0.15.0 §3.13 already had MODULE and PAGE topologies activate after start(), so the imprecision predates v0.15.1 and v0.15.1 §7.2 only made the timing a rule. D1 point 2 and the contract's Registration point 2 were written as one rule, so changing one alone splits the wording. The signal that would have changed my mind: the owner asking for the sharpening, which is then one hsdd-contract touch on topic-codegen@v1 plus the same words in D1 point 2.
